issues.description: The manuscript draws scientific conclusions based on a randomized/dummy dataset. Interpreting random noise as 'no empirical support' or finding 'significant' results in a dummy set is logically invalid and misleading for a scientific report.
issues.quote: We generated a dummy set of samples in the Qualtrics survey (N = 1000) and found no empirical support for the effect of analytical reasoning on the identifiable victim effect.

issues.description: The manuscript states that participants 'selected' their conditions. In an experimental design, participants must be randomly assigned to conditions to ensure internal validity. Self-selection introduces massive confounding variables.
issues.quote: Participants selected their preferred intervention and identifiability conditions.

issues.description: The text describes the study as a 'within-subject design,' but the original study was between-subjects, and the descriptive tables (Table 7) show different sample sizes per cell, which is characteristic of a between-subjects design. Furthermore, if it were within-subjects, the statistical analysis (standard ANOVA) would be inappropriate.
issues.quote: We embedded Studies 1 and 3 of Small et al. (2007) into a single within-subject design

issues.description: The replication uses 'imaginary donation' whereas the original study used real money ($5). Research in JDM shows that hypothetical bias significantly affects prosocial behavior results.
issues.quote: Imaginary donation Participants are required to indicate how much they would donate from $0 to $5 to the corresponding victim(s) instead of donating the money to Save the Children

issues.description: The original study used ordered probit regression, which is appropriate for bounded, discrete monetary data ($0-$5). The replication uses ANOVA, which assumes a continuous normal distribution that donation data (often heavily skewed with many zeros) rarely meets.
issues.quote: Table 5: Comparison of data analysis between the original study and replication... Ordered probit regression... This test would not be conducted in the replication

issues.description: The manuscript contains several placeholders and missing links, indicating it is an incomplete draft.
issues.quote: Cloud folder for presentation (PPT and PDF) | <enter link here>

issues.description: A contributor 'So Chi Liu' is listed in the CRediT taxonomy table but is not included in the author list or affiliations at the beginning of the manuscript.
issues.quote: Role | Yik Chun Wong | Gilad Feldman | So Chi Liu

issues.description: The results section reports p-values and effect sizes for randomized data as if they were meaningful. For example, an interaction effect of p=.015 in a random dataset is a Type I error and should not be interpreted as 'supported'.
issues.quote: Results from Table 9 showed that no significant effect was found on intervention but the identifiability and the interaction effect of identifiability and intervention was supported.

issues.description: The dummy data demographics are highly unrealistic (Mean age 67.8, SD 30.1, Max age 120). While this is dummy data, it suggests the simulation parameters do not reflect the target population (MTurk or students).
issues.quote: Mage = 67.80, SD=30.10; 471 females and 529 males... Age range (years) 18-120

issues.description: The replication removes the 'pre-survey' task where participants earned the money they were later asked to donate. This changes the psychological 'endowment effect'—donating earned money vs. hypothetical money.
issues.quote: No reward acquired from a pre-survey Participants will not conduct an irrelevant survey prior to the experiment to earn $5 for the donation

issues.description: The manuscript refers to 'implicitly learning' about the effect. The original Study 3 was about 'implicit activation' or 'joint evaluation,' not learning. Learning implies explicit knowledge, which contradicts the 'implicit' nature of the manipulation.
issues.quote: Implicitly learning about the identifiable victim effect reduces donations to an identifiable victim

issues.description: The author 'Slovic' is misspelled as 'Solvic' multiple times in the text.
issues.quote: Solvic (2007) argued for the drawbacks of the phenomenon

issues.description: The power analysis is based on the original study's effect sizes (d=0.48). Replication studies should generally power for smaller effects (e.g., 50-75% of the original) due to publication bias in original findings.
issues.quote: The sample size for this study was determined to ensure adequate statistical power for detecting the effects reported in the original study.

issues.description: The manuscript lacks a Discussion section, which is essential for interpreting the (eventual) findings in the context of existing theory.
issues.quote: [The manuscript ends after the Results tables]

issues.description: Updating the victim information to 'most updated' from Save the Children is a deviation that, while necessary for realism, introduces a confound where the severity or nature of the crisis differs from the 2007 original.
issues.quote: We will present the participants with the most updated victim information retrieved from the website of Save the Children

issues.description: The authors state they only conduct post-hoc tests if the interaction is significant. This is a 'gatekeeping' approach that can miss important simple effects or main effects that are theoretically relevant regardless of the interaction.
issues.quote: Note: we conduct the test only if the interaction effect is significant

issues.description: Moving from a physical laboratory/student center to MTurk is a 'Different' physical setting and 'Different' contextual variable that may affect attention and social desirability bias.
issues.quote: Participants will conduct an online survey in Qualtrics on the Mechanical Amazon Turk platform while the original study surveyed inside a student center

issues.description: The authors perform multiple ANOVAs on 'segregated feelings' (Table 13) without mentioning a correction for multiple comparisons (e.g., Bonferroni), increasing the risk of Type I errors.
issues.quote: We conducted a 2 (intervention) X 3 (identifiability) two way ANOVA to examine the effect of identifiability and intervention on segregated affective reactions

issues.description: Table 1 contains 'N/A' for means and SDs of the interaction, which are necessary for a full understanding of the original effect being replicated.
issues.quote: Identifiability* intervention | N/A | N/A

issues.description: There is no mention of Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval or informed consent procedures, which are standard requirements for human subjects research.
issues.quote: [No mention of IRB or Ethics]
